columns.heading: Claude.ai Chat
columns.body: You paste code snippets and describe problems. Claude answers in text. You copy, paste, test, and come back. Context resets each session.

columns.heading: Claude Code
columns.body: Claude reads your actual files, edits them directly, runs commands, and fixes its own errors — all without leaving your terminal or IDE.

columns.heading: The Difference
columns.body: Claude Code is an autonomous coding agent. It doesn't describe solutions — it implements them, verifies them, and iterates until they work.

slides.title: What Claude Code Can Do That Chat Cannot
bullets: Read and edit any file in your project simultaneously
Run shell commands, install packages, start servers
Maintain full context across hundreds of files for an entire session
Catch its own errors and debug them without being asked
Work with git — stage, commit, and write meaningful messages
Call web searches and fetch documentation in real time

slides.title: No Unified View of Bioprocess Data
bullets: DASware OPC UA servers: real-time bioreactor parameters (pH, DO, temp, agitation)
Nova BioProfile Flex2: cell density, viability, metabolites — OPC UA, no history
CEDEX BIO HT: LDH, additional analytes — MAST SQL Server + manual exports
Three disconnected systems, no single dashboard, no trend analysis
Historical data locked in CSV and TXT export files on instrument PCs

slides.title: One Prompt to Start It All
bullets: "Build me a web-based SCADA dashboard for our bioreactors"
No specification document. No architecture diagram.
Just a conversation — and Claude Code figured out the rest.
First working server: within the first hour
slides.caption: The running application — built from a single sentence

slides.title: Discovery
slides.subtitle: Before a line of code was written

slides.title: "Here's the DASware Directory — Figure Out How It Works"
bullets: User copied the entire DASware Connect installation directory to the project folder
Claude read DLL names, XML config files, and log files — no documentation provided
Identified OPC DA (classic COM/DCOM) and OPC UA endpoints from log patterns
Determined exact node-ID naming convention from connection logs: ns=2;s=Plant1/Unit1/...
Confirmed: DASware uses two separate OPC servers per system on port 51530

slides.title: Connected to the LAN — Found Everything
bullets: Claude scanned the lab LAN for OPC UA (port 4840) and SQL Server (port 1433)
Discovered all 8 bioreactor OPC servers: Scivario system at 192.168.137.8, DASbox at 192.168.137.7
Found the MAST SQL Server hosting the CEDEX BIO HT analytical database
Identified Nova BioProfile Flex2 OPC UA server on the instrument PC
No network map, no IT documentation — Claude built the infrastructure map from scratch

slides.title: Claude Browsed the OPC Address Space Live
bullets: Opened a live OPC UA connection to each DASware server
Walked the full node hierarchy — discovered every available tag and its data type
Found the Nova Flex2 node structure (SampleResults, CellDensity, Chem, Gas, Osmo groups)
Used the discovered node IDs to write the polling client — no guesswork, no typos
Built an OPC Tag Browser into the dashboard so operators can re-discover tags themselves

slides.title: "I Don't Have SQL Access — Can You Create a Read-Only Login?"
bullets: Claude identified it couldn't reach the MAST SQL Server without credentials
Rather than guessing or stopping, it asked: "Please create a read-only SQL login for me"
User created the login; Claude connected and explored the schema directly
Found the BioHT join chain: BioHT → SampleData → Vessel → Run → analyte tables
Mapped the VesselId field to bioreactor names and wrote the production SQL query

slides.subtitle: Real inputs — no prompt engineering required

slides.title: You Talk. Claude Code Builds.
bullets: Build me a web-based SCADA dashboard for our bioreactors
Why does it say Invalid Date for the Nova latest measurement?
I copied all the Nova exports to novaexport/ — can you import it all?
Can you add a text filter so it only shows matching sample IDs?
I also have a BioHT txt export — implement the BioHT page just like Nova
The LDH values are not plotting — why?

The server crashed — here is the log
Can you move the Flex2 poll interval into config.json?

slides.eyebrow: What Claude Code Did With Each Prompt
slides.title: From Plain English to Working Code
bullets: Read the existing codebase before touching anything
Traced the bug to a timezone offset format difference (+00:00 vs Z)
Discovered the BioHT timestamp used space not T — Chart.js dropped all points silently
Found the concurrent pyodbc connection race condition from a log paste
Fixed the server crash, added a debounce, and retested — without being asked

slides.title: Key Advantages
slides.subtitle: Why Claude Code changes what's possible

slides.title: Three Things Claude Code Does Differently

columns.heading: Persistent Context
columns.body: Holds your entire codebase in mind for a full session. No re-explaining. No copy-pasting. It knows where everything lives.

columns.heading: Self-Correcting
columns.body: When a bug appears, Claude Code reads the error, finds the root cause, and fixes it — often before you ask. It ran syntax checks after every edit.

columns.heading: Respects Your Constraints
columns.body: "Passwords are never typed in chat" — it remembered this the entire session and never asked. Credentials stayed in .env throughout.

slides.title: What Would Have Taken Weeks Took One Day
bullets: Chat: paste file, get suggestion, paste back, re-run, explain error, repeat
Claude Code: describe the goal once — it reads, edits, verifies, moves on
Cross-file changes (e.g., add a feature to backend + frontend + config) in one step
Git history created automatically with meaningful commit messages
No context lost when switching between database, API, and UI work

slides.title: The Same Pattern in Two Different Domains

columns.heading: SCADA Dashboard
bullets: Plan: Analyze OPC logs, map network topology, design DB schema
Build: FastAPI backend, OPC UA client, Chart.js frontend
Test: Playwright automates browser, takes screenshots
Read: Claude sees exactly what the user sees — every bug visible
Fix: Edit code, restart server, re-run Playwright automatically
Key tool: Playwright + asyncua + network access

columns.heading: This Presentation
bullets: Plan: Outline content, pick slide types, choose icons
Build: Write deck.json spec, run build_pptx.py
Test: pptx_verify.py renders every slide to PNG via LibreOffice
Read: Claude reads each PNG — sees layout, overflow, spacing
Fix: Edit deck.json, rebuild PPTX, re-run verify automatically
Key tool: merck-ppt-v2 skill + LibreOffice headless

slides.title: Automated Testing Is What Closes the Loop
bullets: Without Playwright: Claude describes solutions — but cannot see whether the UI actually works
Without pptx_verify: Claude writes a spec — but cannot see whether the slide renders correctly
With these tools: Claude finds the issue, locates the cause, fixes it, and verifies the fix — without stopping
This is the difference between an AI that helps and an AI that delivers
The more tools Claude can run and read, the more autonomously it can iterate

Iterates: adjust volumes, aspiration rates, tip types based on measured transfer accuracy
End goal: autonomous protocol optimization — no manual iteration between runs

slides.eyebrow: Why This Is the Same Pattern
slides.title: The Test Loop Extends to Physical Systems
bullets: The Opentrons Python API is Claude Code's actuator — it can run any protocol
The plate reader is Claude Code's test harness — measurable, repeatable output
Plate reader result → Claude reads data → identifies deviation → updates protocol → re-run
What took a scientist a day of manual iteration could complete overnight autonomously
This is not hypothetical — the SCADA dashboard was built by the same closed loop today
